output.review_comment:
The two fixes to `periods` (ceiling division) and rounding (`+5000` before `//10000`) are correct and match every test case, including the half-up rounding case (34100, 20) -> 512 and the "started period" semantics.

However, the third change — swapping the order of the cap and the minimum — is a problem, and the PR description itself admits why: it was made "only so that `test_small_balance_pays_minimum` passes," and it directly contradicts the docstring, which explicitly states the fee is (1) computed, (2) raised to the minimum, (3) capped at 1/5 of balance, and that "the cap always wins, even when it brings the fee below the minimum fee." The new code does the opposite (cap first, then minimum can push the fee back up above the cap), so for the (1800, 45) case the minimum now wins over the cap — the exact opposite of what the docstring promises.

Since the teammate said the tests encode the agreed spec, it's fine to conform the code to the tests, but the docstring must be updated to accurately describe the new (minimum-wins) ordering — right now the code and its own documentation directly contradict each other, which will mislead the next person who reads it (and arguably means finance's documented rule was actually implemented backwards prior to this PR, or the test/docstring disagree and someone should confirm which is intended before merging). At minimum, update steps 2/3 and the "cap always wins" sentence in the docstring to match the implemented behavior. I'd also flag this ordering ambiguity back to the teammate/finance rather than silently resolving it, since it's a business-rule detail, not just a code fix.

Please update the docstring to match the new min/cap ordering before merging.
